ncc_references.relationship: Performance pathway that calls up residential timber-framing standards.
Framing section scope; detailed timber framing is referenced through Volume Two H1D6.

objects.name: timber wall frame
objects.definition: The structural timber skeleton of a wall, assembled from plates, studs, opening members, noggings and any required bracing.
functions: Carry vertical loads where the wall is loadbearing
Provide a stable base for linings, claddings, openings and insulation
Transfer bracing forces to the structure below

cad.placement: On the floor or supporting structure along the wall path
cad.opening: Contains framed door and window openings

objects.name: timber floor frame
objects.definition: The supporting timber skeleton below a floor surface, commonly including bearers, joists, trimming members and blocking.
functions: Support floor loads
Transfer floor loads to walls, posts, piers or foundations
Provide a fixing base for flooring

cad.placement: Between the floor surface and its supporting walls, posts, piers or foundations
cad.opening: May be trimmed around floor openings

objects.name: conventional timber roof frame
objects.definition: A roof structure built on site from individual rafters, ceiling joists, beams, struts, underpurlins, ties and ridge members rather than prefabricated trusses.
functions: Support the roof covering and ceiling
Transfer roof loads to walls and other supports
Tie and brace the roof into a stable structure

cad.placement: Above supporting walls
cad.opening: May be trimmed around roof and ceiling openings

notes: A coupled roof is a particular structural arrangement and should not automatically be treated as an exact synonym for every conventional roof frame.

objects.name: nailplated timber roof truss
objects.definition: A prefabricated triangulated timber roof unit whose chords and webs are joined at nodes, commonly with pressed metal nailplates.
functions: Span between supports
Support roof and ceiling loads
Transfer loads through triangulated members to supporting walls or beams

cad.pattern: Repeated parallel units at designed centres
cad.placement: On supporting walls or beams
cad.start: First truss or gable support line
cad.end: Last truss or gable support line
cad.opening: Special trusses and framing may be required around openings

notes: Member sizes, nailplate layouts and permitted modifications are design matters; the ontology does not infer them.

objects.name: top plate
objects.definition: A horizontal timber member fixed along the top of a wall frame, including across framed openings.
functions: Tie the tops of studs together
Distribute loads from rafters, trusses or upper framing into the wall

cad.pattern: Continuous run with designed joints
cad.placement: Along the top edge of the wall
cad.opening: Usually continues over openings
cad.load: Distributes roof, floor or upper-wall loads

objects.name: bottom plate
objects.definition: The lowest horizontal timber member of a wall frame, fixed to the floor or supporting structure beneath it.
functions: Tie the bottoms of studs together
Locate and fix the wall frame
Transfer wall loads to the structure below

cad.pattern: Continuous run interrupted where designed
cad.placement: Along the bottom edge of the wall
cad.opening: May continue through or be cut at door openings according to construction sequence
cad.load: Transfers stud and wall loads downward

objects.name: common stud
objects.definition: A full-height vertical wall member placed at regular centres away from the specialised framing at openings and intersections.
functions: Support the top plate
Transfer vertical loads to the bottom plate
Provide fixing for wall linings and claddings

cad.pattern: Repeated at nominated centres
cad.placement: Between bottom and top plates
cad.opening: Regular pattern is interrupted at openings
cad.load: May carry vertical compression and lining loads

objects.name: jamb stud
objects.definition: A full-height vertical stud forming one side of a framed door or window opening.
functions: Form the side boundary of an opening
Support opening members and provide fixing for the door or window assembly

cad.pattern: One or more full-height members at each side of an opening
cad.placement: At the vertical side of a framed opening
cad.opening: Defines the opening jamb
cad.load: May support lintel and wall loads depending on design

notes: The possible alias 'king stud' is quarantined for review because it is not the preferred Australian term in the sources used.

objects.name: jack stud
objects.definition: A shortened vertical stud installed above or below a wall opening between a plate and an opening trimmer or lintel.
functions: Maintain the wall stud layout around an opening
Support or connect the framing immediately above or below the opening

cad.pattern: Continues the nominated stud layout where space permits
cad.placement: Above a lintel or below a sill trimmer
cad.opening: Occupies the wall area immediately above or below the opening

notes: Some sources use 'jack stud' for a stud supporting a lintel end. That conflicting usage is not accepted here without further Australian evidence.

objects.name: lintel
objects.definition: A horizontal structural member spanning over a door, window or other wall opening.
functions: Carry wall, floor or roof loads over an opening
Transfer those loads to supporting framing at each side

cad.pattern: One designed member or built-up set per loadbearing opening
cad.placement: Directly over an opening
cad.end: Bearing at the other opening jamb
cad.opening: Spans across the opening head

objects.name: sill trimmer
objects.definition: A horizontal member forming the bottom edge of a framed window opening between its jamb studs.
functions: Form the lower boundary of the rough opening
Support short studs and provide fixing below a window

cad.pattern: One at the base of each framed window opening
cad.placement: Between jamb studs at the window sill level
cad.opening: Defines the bottom of the rough opening
cad.load: Supports local framing and window loads

notes: Do not confuse this framing member with the visible finished sill of a window assembly.

objects.name: head trimmer
objects.definition: A horizontal framing member forming the top edge of a non-loadbearing wall opening where a structural lintel is not performing that role.
functions: Form the upper boundary of a rough opening
Provide fixing and support for short framing above the opening

cad.pattern: One at the head of a framed non-loadbearing opening where required
cad.placement: Between jamb framing at opening-head level
cad.opening: Defines the top of the rough opening
cad.load: Carries local framing only unless specifically designed otherwise

notes: Kept distinct from a structural lintel; exact Australian usage needs another authoritative source before full acceptance.

objects.name: nogging
objects.definition: A short horizontal timber member fitted between adjacent wall studs, normally in one or more rows.
functions: Provide lateral restraint to studs
Help keep studs aligned
Provide fixing where required

cad.pattern: Repeated between studs in aligned or staggered rows
cad.placement: Between adjacent studs
cad.opening: Pattern stops or changes at openings

objects.name: wall brace
objects.definition: A diagonal strap, timber member or structural sheet arrangement fixed to a wall frame to resist sideways forces.
functions: Keep the wall frame square and stable
Transfer racking forces caused by wind and other actions

cad.pattern: Located in nominated bracing wall panels
cad.placement: Fixed across or within a wall frame
cad.opening: Requires adequate unbroken wall panel

notes: Geometry depends on whether the brace is a strap, timber diagonal or structural sheet system.

objects.name: bearer
objects.definition: A horizontal primary floor member supported by posts, stumps, piers, walls or foundations and carrying floor joists above.
functions: Support floor joists
Transfer floor loads to the supporting structure below

cad.pattern: Parallel primary members at designed spacing
cad.placement: On posts, stumps, piers, walls or foundations below the joists

objects.name: floor joist
objects.definition: A repeated horizontal floor member that spans between supports and carries flooring and floor loads.
functions: Support the floor surface and imposed loads
Transfer those loads to bearers, walls or beams

cad.pattern: Repeated parallel members at nominated centres
cad.placement: Across bearers, walls or beams and usually perpendicular to bearers
cad.opening: Cut joists terminate at trimming members

objects.name: trimming joist
objects.definition: A joist beside a floor opening that receives the ends of one or more cut joists or trimmers and carries their loads to supports.
functions: Form a structural side of a floor opening
Support members interrupted by the opening

cad.pattern: Located at designed sides of a floor opening
cad.placement: Alongside the opening and parallel to the main joists where applicable
cad.opening: Defines and supports one side of a framed floor opening
cad.load: Carries concentrated reactions from interrupted framing

objects.name: floor joist solid blocking
objects.definition: Short solid pieces fitted tightly between adjacent floor joists to restrain them and help distribute local effects.
functions: Restrain deep joists from rolling or twisting
Maintain joist spacing and alignment

cad.pattern: Rows between adjacent joists where restraint is required
cad.placement: Tightly between floor joists
cad.opening: Pattern changes around openings
cad.load: Lateral restraint rather than a primary spanning member

objects.name: ceiling joist
objects.definition: A horizontal roof-space member that supports the ceiling and, in a coupled roof, ties the lower ends of opposing rafters.
functions: Support ceiling loads
Tie opposing walls or rafter feet where the roof arrangement relies on that action

cad.pattern: Repeated parallel members at nominated centres
cad.placement: At ceiling level between supporting walls
cad.opening: Trimmed around ceiling openings where required
cad.load: Supports ceiling; may act as a tension tie

objects.name: hanging beam
objects.definition: A roof-space beam placed above and generally at right angles to ceiling joists so the joists can be suspended from it and have a shorter effective span.
functions: Support ceiling joists from above
Reduce the effective span of ceiling joists

cad.pattern: Placed where ceiling joist span needs intermediate support
cad.placement: Above and usually perpendicular to ceiling joists
cad.load: Ceiling load only unless specifically designed for more

notes: Do not place roof struts on a hanging beam unless it has been specifically designed for that load.

objects.name: strutting beam
objects.definition: A roof-space beam designed to receive roof struts and transfer their concentrated loads to loadbearing supports without loading the ceiling joists below.
functions: Support roof struts
Transfer roof loads to loadbearing walls or other designed supports

cad.pattern: Located below designed roof-strut positions
cad.placement: Above ceiling joists and spanning between loadbearing supports

objects.name: roof strut
objects.definition: A compression member installed between an underpurlin and a strutting beam or loadbearing wall to carry roof loads downward.
functions: Support an underpurlin
Transfer roof loads to a suitable bearing point below

cad.pattern: Located at designed support points along an underpurlin
cad.placement: Between underpurlin and strutting beam or loadbearing support

objects.name: underpurlin
objects.definition: A horizontal or near-horizontal roof member placed under and across rafters to give them intermediate support.
functions: Support rafters between ridge and wall plate
Transfer rafter loads to struts, walls or other designed supports

cad.pattern: Runs across a group of rafters at designed roof-slope positions
cad.placement: Against the underside of rafters and approximately parallel to the ridge

objects.name: collar tie
objects.definition: A horizontal timber member fixed between a pair of opposing rafters above the wall plates.
functions: Tie opposing rafters together
Help restrain rafter spread or separation according to the roof arrangement

cad.pattern: Repeated at nominated rafter pairs
cad.placement: Between opposing rafters

objects.name: common rafter
objects.definition: A repeated sloping roof member running from a wall plate or eaves support towards the ridge.
functions: Support roof battens and covering
Transfer roof loads to walls, ridge support and any intermediate underpurlins

cad.pattern: Repeated parallel sloping members at nominated centres
cad.placement: From top plate or eaves support to ridge
cad.start: Wall top plate or eaves support
cad.opening: Cut or trimmed around roof openings

objects.name: ridgeboard
objects.definition: A longitudinal board at the roof ridge used to locate, align and connect the upper ends of opposing rafters.
functions: Provide a common fixing line for rafter tops
Keep opposing rafter ends aligned during framing

cad.pattern: Continuous run with joints where required
cad.placement: Along the roof ridge between opposing rafters
cad.load: Set-out and connection member unless specifically designed as a beam

notes: A ridgeboard is not automatically a loadbearing ridge beam.

objects.name: hip rafter
objects.definition: A diagonal sloping rafter forming the external intersection of two roof planes and receiving shortened rafters from both sides.
functions: Form and support a roof hip
Receive jack rafters from adjoining roof planes

cad.pattern: One along each external roof-plane intersection
cad.placement: Diagonally from an external wall corner to the ridge end
cad.load: Diagonal roof beam receiving jack rafters

notes: Definition is accepted pending a stronger dedicated Australian public source.

objects.name: jack rafter
objects.definition: A shortened sloping rafter that runs between a wall plate and a hip rafter, or between a ridge and a valley rafter.
functions: Support roof battens and covering in a hip or valley area
Transfer roof loads to the hip or valley member and other support

cad.pattern: Repeated shortened members stepping along hip or valley
cad.placement: Between wall plate and hip, or ridge and valley

notes: Creeper rafter usage varies; it is not accepted as an exact synonym in this pilot.

objects.name: truss top chord
objects.definition: A sloping outer member forming the top edge of a roof truss and carrying roof battens and roof loads into the truss nodes.
functions: Support roof battens and covering
Carry compression or combined forces between truss nodes

cad.pattern: Usually a pair forming the upper truss profile
cad.placement: Along the sloping upper boundary of the truss

objects.name: truss bottom chord
objects.definition: The lower outer member of a roof truss, commonly horizontal, connecting the truss heels and supporting ceiling loads where designed.
functions: Complete the lower side of the truss triangle
Carry designed tension and ceiling loads

cad.pattern: One lower chord line per truss profile
cad.placement: Along the lower boundary of the truss
cad.load: Designed truss chord and possible ceiling support

objects.name: truss web
objects.definition: An internal timber member connecting truss chords at nodes and dividing the truss into stable triangular panels.
functions: Transfer forces between top and bottom chords
Maintain the triangulated truss form

cad.pattern: Arranged between chord nodes to the engineered truss design
cad.placement: Inside the truss outline

objects.name: truss web tie
objects.definition: A longitudinal timber restraint fixed across corresponding web members in a run of roof trusses.
functions: Restrain selected truss webs laterally
Link the restraint of one truss to the braced roof system

cad.pattern: Continuous or lapped run across nominated webs
cad.placement: Perpendicular to the truss planes on specified web faces

objects.name: truss nailplate
objects.definition: A toothed sheet-steel connector pressed into the faces of timber members at a truss node to join them together.
functions: Connect timber truss members at a node
Transfer designed forces between the connected members

cad.pattern: Usually applied to both faces at each designed truss node
cad.placement: Centred over member intersections at truss nodes

notes: Plate size and position are fabrication-design data and must not be guessed by a drawing tool.

objects.name: roof batten
objects.definition: A small repeated member fixed across rafters or truss top chords to support and secure the roof covering.
functions: Support roof tiles or sheet roofing
Transfer roof-covering loads and wind forces to rafters or trusses

cad.pattern: Repeated parallel rows at covering-specific spacing
cad.placement: Across rafters or truss top chords
cad.opening: Trimmed and supported around penetrations as designed
cad.load: Supports roof covering and transfers wind actions

objects.name: truncated girder truss
objects.definition: A shortened flat-topped girder truss in a hip-roof truss system that carries loads from supported hip and jack trusses.
functions: Provide the main support line in a hip-truss set
Receive concentrated loads from supported trusses

cad.pattern: Located at the designed girder position in a hip-truss set
cad.placement: Across the building near the start of the hipped roof zone

objects.name: hip truss
objects.definition: A truss used in a prefabricated hip-roof set to form or support the sloping hip portion of the roof.
functions: Form part of the hipped roof geometry
Support roof framing and covering in the hip zone

cad.pattern: Placed at its scheduled position in the hip-truss set
cad.placement: Within the hipped end of a trussed roof

objects.name: jack truss
objects.definition: A shortened roof truss in a hip-roof set that is supported at one end by a girder truss or associated hip framing.
functions: Support roof loads in the hip zone
Transfer loads to the girder truss and external support

cad.pattern: A stepped sequence of shortened trusses in the hip zone
cad.placement: Between external wall support and girder or hip framing
cad.end: Girder truss or designed hip support

objects.name: creeper truss
objects.definition: A small or shortened truss used near a hipped roof end to complete the roof surface between larger trusses and the end framing.
functions: Support roof loads near the hipped end
Complete the stepped truss layout at the diminishing roof width

cad.pattern: Stepped sequence at the hipped end according to the truss layout
cad.placement: Near the hipped end of a trussed roof
cad.end: Hip or truss support as designed

notes: Creeper-truss and jack-truss labels should follow the fabricator's truss layout rather than geometric guesswork.

objects.name: roof truss brace
objects.definition: A permanent diagonal or longitudinal member fixed across a run of roof trusses to stabilise them as a group and transfer restraint forces.
functions: Restrain trusses against movement out of their plane
Transfer stability forces to braced points in the building

cad.pattern: Installed across nominated trusses to the bracing layout
cad.placement: On chord or web planes as specified

notes: Temporary erection bracing is a different object and is outside this pilot.
